headline: Election-week caution splits the market: value steady, chips correct
body: Election day brought a split tape rather than a unified move: the Dow added roughly 0.4% on continued rotation into value names, while the S&P 500 slipped about half a percent and the Nasdaq fell over 1% as tech and semiconductors took the hit. The Nasdaq 100 is now down around 10% from its late-year highs, a textbook technical correction, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index off more than 3% on the day. Marvell led chip losses after unveiling a roughly $115 billion deal to acquire Lumentum, while Intel and Oracle each fell nearly 9%. Apple slipped in premarket trading after beating on iPhone demand but missing on Greater China revenue. None of this reads as panic — it looks more like continued digestion of a crowded AI trade against a backdrop of real event risk: midterm election results and AMD's earnings were the two catalysts investors were most explicitly positioning around heading into the session.

The macro backdrop adds a layer of caution rather than relief. The Fed held rates steady at 3.75%-4.00% at its late-October meeting on a split 10-2 vote, with two dissenters pushing for a hike rather than a cut, and futures markets are now pricing meaningful odds of a rate increase in December rather than further easing — a reversal from the cutting-cycle narrative that dominated earlier in the year. That lines up with elevated crude prices near $110 a barrel and a heavy data calendar (payrolls this week, CPI next week) that leaves little room for a dovish surprise. Retail and social-media chatter offered no distinct signal today beyond the usual chip-stock focus, so this read leans on price action and the earnings/macro calendar rather than forum sentiment. Overall tone: selective risk-off in the most AI-exposed corners of the market, with money rotating toward value and away from re-rating hawkish-rate risk, rather than a broad flight from equities.
